content:
# Get Element By Id

The `document.getElementById()` method finds one element on the page by matching its `id`. Use it when your JavaScript needs to select a specific button, paragraph, image, or other page element.
examples: [{"name":"Select a Button","description":"This selects the button with the `id` `\"buttonOne\"`.","code":"`const buttonOne = document.getElementById(\"buttonOne\");`","app":""},{"name":"Change Text on the Page","description":"This selects a paragraph and changes the text shown on the page.","code":"`const message = document.getElementById(\"message\");`\n\n`message.textContent = \"Hello!\";`"}]
name: Get Element By Id
tips:
- `document.getElementById()` is used to select one element from the HTML page.
- The `id` inside the parentheses must match an `id` in your HTML.
- Put quotation marks around the `id` name.
- Do not include the `#` symbol. Use `"buttonOne"`, not `"#buttonOne"`.
- In Web Lab, this method often appears near the top of `script.js` to store page elements in variables.
